refnamediv.refpurpose: Configuration for device event managing daemon

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: These files contain configuration options for udevd8. The syntax of these files is very simple: a list of assignments, one per line. All empty lines or lines beginning with # are ignored.

The main configuration file is the first udev.conf found in /etc/udev, /run/udev, /usr/local/lib/udev and /usr/lib/udev (or /lib/udev, depending on the build, and both when built with --enable-split-usr), in this order. The drop-ins, the files with the extension .conf in the udev.conf.d subdirectories of these directories, are read after it, sorted by their names, regardless of the directories in which they live. A setting overrides the same setting in the files read before. A drop-in replaces the drop-ins with the same name in the directories listed after its own: one in /etc replaces those in /run, /usr/local/lib and /usr/lib; a symlink to /dev/null or an empty file disables them. Files that are not regular files are ignored. A program that uses libudev, like udevd and udevadm, reads the files once, when it creates its first libudev context, and again for the next context only when they could not be read completely, e.g. when a file could not be opened.
The following options can be set:

listitem.para: The log level. Valid values are the numerical syslog priorities or their textual representations: err, info and debug.

note.para: This option is also honored by udevadm8.

listitem.para: An integer. The maximum number of events executed in parallel. When unspecified or 0 is specified, the maximum is determined based on the system resources: MIN(2 × CPUs + 16, MAX(RAM / 128 MiB, 10), 2048), where CPUs is the number of CPUs udevd may run on, according to its CPU affinity, and RAM the size of the physical memory, or the memory limit of the cgroup of PID 1 when it is smaller: memory.max with cgroup v2, or memory.limit_in_bytes in the hierarchy of the memory controller with cgroup v1.
This is the same as the --children-max= option of udevd8.

Delay the execution of RUN instructions by the given number of seconds, or by a time span with a unit, e.g. 500ms. This option might be useful when debugging system crashes during coldplug caused by loading non-working kernel modules. 0 means no delay, and a delay that is not shorter than the event timeout is ignored.
This is the same as the --exec-delay= option of udevd8.

The number of seconds to wait for events to finish, or a time span with a unit, e.g. 5min. After this time, the event will be terminated. The default is 180 seconds, which is also used when 0 or less than a millisecond is given.
This is the same as the --event-timeout= option of udevd8.

Specifies when udevd should resolve names of users and groups. When set to early (the default), names will be resolved when the rules are parsed. When set to late, names will be resolved for every event. When set to never, names will never be resolved, and the OWNER and GROUP keys whose value is not a numeric ID, i.e. a name or a value with substitutions, will be ignored; the other keys of these rules still apply.
This is the same as the --resolve-names= option of udevd8.
The format of the compiled hardware database hwdb.bin created by udevadm hwdb --update. Valid values are 1 and 2, invalid values are ignored with a warning. Defaults to 1.

Format 1 is the compatible format, which can be read by all versions of libudev. When a device matches multiple entries of the hardware database which set the same property, it is undefined which of the values is used.

Format 2 additionally stores the origin (the source file and the line number) of every property, so that for the same property the value from a later file or a later line takes precedence. This format can only be read by libudev from this release or newer: older versions of libudev, including an old udevd which was not restarted after an upgrade, misread such a database.
When udevadm hwdb --update is used with --root=, the value is taken from udev.conf below the specified root directory instead, and defaults to 1 if it is not set there.

Takes a boolean argument (yes, true, 1 or no, false, 0). Defaults to no. Selects how the path_id builtin composes the SAS part of ID_PATH, and thus the /dev/disk/by-path/ links, of devices behind a SAS port whose num_phys attribute is not 1.

By default only ports with two or more phys are treated as wide ports and named after the SAS address of the end device: sas-0xADDRESS-lun-N. Ports reporting zero phys, as done e.g. by the smartpqi driver, are named like single phy ports after the phy they are connected to: sas-phyPHY-lun-N, or sas-exp0xADDRESS-phyPHY-lun-N when connected through an expander. If num_phys cannot be parsed, no ID_PATH is set.

If set to yes, the naming of older eudev versions is used: every port with a num_phys other than 1, including 0 and unparsable values, is treated as a wide port and named sas-0xADDRESS-lun-N. This keeps existing by-path links of such controllers stable. The file is only read when udevd starts, and the links of already present devices are updated only when their events are processed again, e.g. by udevadm trigger.

Takes a boolean argument. Defaults to yes. When set to no, OPTIONS+="net_altnames" is ignored, i.e. no alternative names are assigned to network interfaces, which 80-net-altnames.rules requests by default (see udev7). An invalid or empty value is ignored, with a warning whenever the configuration is read: when udevd starts, and by udevadm test. udevd only reads the file when it starts, and alternative names are only assigned when an interface is added.

Selects the naming scheme used by the net_id builtin to generate the predictable names of network interfaces: eudev for the names generated by the net_id builtin of eudev 3.2.15 and older, one of the schemes of systemd, e.g. v255, or latest, the default. The schemes are described in udev7. Setting it keeps these names stable when a new version adds a new scheme. It does not select the rules that choose the name an interface is renamed to, which are the same with all schemes, e.g. the name from the hwdb is preferred, and interfaces named by userspace or predictably by the kernel are not renamed, also with eudev. net.naming_scheme= on the kernel command line and the $NET_NAMING_SCHEME environment variable of udevd, unless its value starts with :, take precedence (see udevd8). Unknown names are ignored with a warning, and the next setting in that order is used. The file is only read when udevd starts, and interfaces are renamed only when they are added, so a change takes effect at the next boot; also rebuild the initrd if it starts udevd.

Specifies a signal that udevd will send on worker timeouts. Note that both workers and spawned processes will be killed using this signal. Defaults to SIGKILL. This is the same as the --timeout-signal= option of udevd8. An invalid value is ignored, with a warning when udevd starts. This includes the signals whose default action does not terminate a process, with which the timeout would not stop anything: SIGCHLD, SIGCONT, SIGSTOP, SIGTSTP, SIGTTIN, SIGTTOU, SIGURG and SIGWINCH. A worker that has not finished its event 5 seconds after the signal is killed with SIGKILL; after a signal whose default action dumps core, e.g. SIGABRT, 90 seconds, so that the core dump is not cut off.

refsect1.para: In addition, udevd can be configured by command-line options and the kernel command line (see udevd8). The command-line options take precedence over the settings in this file, the options on the kernel command line take precedence over both, and for the maximum number of workers, udevadm control --children-max= over all of them. For children_max, exec_delay and event_timeout, 0 counts as not set, so e.g. udev.children_max=0 on the kernel command line does not override children_max=4 in this file. Invalid values of children_max, exec_delay, event_timeout and resolve_names are ignored, with a warning when udevd starts. The files are only read when udevd starts.
